name: Kenya
summary: The Kenyan embassy or high commission in the country of death issues a no objection letter for the remains once it has the death certificate, local burial or transit permit, non-contagious disease letter and embalming letter. The letter is free and some missions issue it within one day.
documents: Proof of Kenyan nationality of the deceased (passport, ID card or birth certificate) where applicable
Certified copy of the death certificate
Locally issued burial and/or transit permit (in the UK: Out of England certificate)
Letter from the local health authority that the death was not from a contagious disease
Letter from the funeral director confirming and describing the embalming
No objection letter from the Kenyan embassy or high commission
coffin: Kenyan missions recommend a sealable casket; the Kenyan Embassy in Washington recommends a metal, hermetically sealable casket. Airline packaging rules also apply. No witnessing of the sealing by a Kenyan official is required by the published checklists.
embalming: Required: missions ask for a funeral director's letter confirming embalming; the London High Commission asks that it state embalming in line with ICAO and international guidelines.
consular: The Kenyan mission issues a no objection letter for transport of the remains, given to the shipping company. No fee is charged. The Kenya Embassy in Spain states one working day once documents are complete. Names and dates must match on all documents, or approvals are delayed. Not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement 1973, so a mortuary laissez-passer alone is not enough.
arrival: Remains are cleared by customs and port health at the arrival airport and released to the family or their funeral home. Ministry of Health clearance was specifically required for COVID-19 related remains (2021 protocol); confirm whether it still applies to infectious-disease deaths.
private_aviation: No Kenyan rules specific to private flights carrying remains were published. Land at an international airport with customs and port health (Nairobi JKIA or Mombasa) and carry the original no objection letter and documents with the casket.
private_jet_note: Use an airport with customs and port health; carry the original no objection letter.
export: To send a body out of Kenya, the death is registered with the Civil Registration Office or a Huduma centre (burial permit, death certificate in English showing the cause). Polish consular guidance lists the Kenyan documents usually issued: burial permit from local authorities, certificate of no infectious disease and embalming certificate. Deaths outside hospital are reported to police and a post-mortem may be needed, which can delay release. The destination country's embassy may need to issue its own entry authorisation.
export_points: Register the death and obtain the burial permit
Embalming certificate and no infectious disease certificate
Police report and post-mortem for sudden or violent deaths
Destination embassy authorisation if required

at_a_glance.consular: Free no objection letter from mission

steps.what: Death certificate and appointment of a funeral director in the country of death.
Embalming, non-contagious disease letter and local burial or transit permit.
Send the documents to the Kenyan embassy or high commission for the no objection letter.

key_points: No objection letter is free of charge
Name and date mismatches between documents cause delays
Metal hermetically sealable casket recommended
authority: Kenyan embassy or high commission in the country of death; Ministry of Health (port health) on arrival

name: Lesotho
summary: No official Lesotho checklist for incoming remains was found. UK guidance states that no airlines operate repatriation services from Lesotho and bodies travel by hearse via O.R. Tambo airport in Johannesburg, so incoming caskets normally route through South Africa and must also meet South African transit rules.
documents: Death certificate (English translation if needed)
Embalming certificate
Certificate of non-contagious disease (confirm)
Coffin sealing certificate
Permits required by South Africa for transit by road (confirm with South African authorities)
Passport or ID of the deceased
Any authorisation required by the Lesotho high commission or embassy (not published)
coffin: For repatriation from Lesotho, UK guidance describes a hermetically sealed zinc coffin placed in a packing crate. No official Lesotho specification for incoming coffins was found; follow the same standard.
embalming: UK guidance states the body must be embalmed within 3 days of death for repatriation out of Lesotho. No published rule for incoming remains; embalming is expected by airlines.
consular: The role of Lesotho's missions for incoming remains is not published; contact the Lesotho high commission or embassy. Not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement 1973, so a mortuary laissez-passer alone is not enough.
arrival: Remains usually arrive at O.R. Tambo (Johannesburg) and travel by road to Lesotho, crossing the border with a hearse. Lesotho has no cremation facilities.
private_aviation: No published rules for private flights carrying remains into Lesotho. A private flight may land in Johannesburg with onward road transfer; landing in Lesotho itself depends on airport customs and handling availability and must be confirmed.
private_jet_note: Commercial repatriation routes via Johannesburg; confirm customs handling before landing in Lesotho.
export: Register the death at the National Identity and Civil Registry office of the district. A post-mortem by state pathologists is required for unnatural deaths. The body must be embalmed within 3 days of death, placed in a hermetically sealed zinc coffin in a packing crate, and driven to O.R. Tambo airport in Johannesburg; the funeral director needs a letter from the next of kin consenting to cross-border transport. Documents: civil registry death certificate, embalming certificate and certificate permitting transfer of the remains.
export_points: Embalming within 3 days of death
Hermetically sealed zinc coffin in packing crate
Road transfer to Johannesburg airport
Next of kin consent letter for border crossing
